intent: Administrators monitor public page views and unique tab sessions; suppliers monitor only their own profile/product traffic. Use 7/30/90 UTC days, one view per path/session/day, all consent, hashed session IDs, public paths only, exclude admin/self visits, and preserve legacy product history. Verified server sessions authorize reports; service_role alone calls SQL RPCs. Migration additive and not deployed.

testing_gaps: PageViewTracker has no checked-in lifecycle tests for denied consent, consent granted after mount, revocation before navigation, blocked storage, or listener cleanup on path changes; the supplied browser evidence covers only positive consent.
Traffic tests do not seed historical viewed_on values: the UTC next-day deduplication behavior and inclusive 7/30/90-day cutoff boundaries remain unverified.
The legacy history test starts with an empty product_views table for its product, so it proves new traffic mirroring but not preservation and aggregation of pre-existing legacy product history.
